findings.sourceQuote: COL4A1 and COL4A2 encode type IV collagen, a principal structural component of basement membranes, and pathogenic variants in these genes cause a multisystem small vessel vasculopathy with prominent cerebrovascular involvement.

findings.sourceQuote: We also provide new insights into the role of type IV collagen-related genes, specifically serpinh1b , col4a1, and col4a2 , which were downregulated in our model.

findings.causalEvidenceSummary: Known monogenic cSVD gene with new functional data. Deleting Col4a1 in the brain endothelium of adult mice caused dose-dependent, progressive cerebral microbleeds that resembled the human distribution. The mice also showed basement membrane thinning, cognitive decline and motor incoordination. The paper argues that disrupted collagen IV homeostasis underlies sporadic CMBs.
findings.sourceQuote: This work provides the first animal model demonstrating that selective disruption of collagen IV in adult brain microvessels is sufficient to generate CMBs with high penetrance and dose-dependent tunability.

findings.causalEvidenceSummary: Case report: a woman in her late 50s with a family history of young-onset stroke had a large left parietal-temporal (lobar) haematoma and microhaemorrhages on the opposite side of the brain. Genetic testing confirmed a pathogenic COL4A2 mutation, consistent with hereditary (monogenic) cSVD. This is new patient-level evidence, not a background citation, but it comes from a single case with no population-level or functional data.
findings.sourceQuote: Subsequent genetic testing confirmed a pathogenic COL4A2 mutation, consistent with hereditary cerebral small vessel disease.

findings.causalEvidenceSummary: Family case report: a Japanese father and son with lacunar infarction, multiple WMH and intracranial artery dilation/tortuosity carried a distal 13q34 duplication that includes COL4A1 and COL4A2. The authors attribute the cSVD to the duplication, which adds new family-level evidence for a known monogenic gene. It is a copy-number variant spanning both genes, so the effect cannot be assigned to COL4A1 alone.
findings.sourceQuote: Our cases suggest that dilation and tortuosity of the multiple intracranial artery may be a distinguishing neuroradiological feature of patients with CSVD caused by COL4A1/COL4A2 duplication.

findings.causalEvidenceSummary: Family case report: a distal 13q34 duplication that includes COL4A1 and COL4A2 was found in a father and son with lacunar infarction, multiple WMH and intracranial artery dilation/tortuosity. The authors consider it the cause of hereditary cSVD. Because the copy-number variant spans both genes, the effect cannot be assigned to COL4A2 alone.
findings.sourceQuote: Our cases suggest that dilation and tortuosity of the multiple intracranial artery may be a distinguishing neuroradiological feature of patients with CSVD caused by COL4A1/COL4A2 duplication.

It was found in a patient with recurrent ischemic stroke and infarcts in the centrum semiovale, basal ganglia, thalamus and brainstem, consistent with COL4A1/COL4A2-related hereditary cSVD. This is new CNV evidence for a known monogenic cSVD gene. However, the duplication spans many genes and is reported in one patient only.
findings.sourceQuote: Whole-exome sequencing identified a pathogenic 13.4‑Mb duplication at 13q32.2‑q34, encompassing the COL4A1 and COL4A2 loci, consistent with the molecular diagnostic criteria for COL4A1/COL4A2-related hCSVD.

findings.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cSVD gene. This paper adds new rare-variant data: trio exome sequencing found biallelic COL4A2 variants in two unrelated cases with brain small vessel disease (BSVD) or cerebrovascular defects and cortical malformations. These were a homozygous p.(Arg179Cys) variant, classified as likely benign (ACMG Class II) but predicted to destabilise the protein, and compound heterozygous c.826-1G>T and p.(Gly1426Argfs*30) variants, both likely pathogenic loss-of-function. In silico protein modelling (ThermoMPNN, Rosetta, AlphaMissense) supports a destabilising effect for Arg179Cys. This is case-level Mendelian evidence, not GWAS.
findings.sourceQuote: In conclusion, our study emphasizes the critical role of biallelic COL4A2 variants in BSVD and severe brain malformations, significantly expanding the genotype and phenotype spectrum of recessive COL4A2‐related disorders.

The authors say this confirms that these copy number gains are pathogenic, likely through gene dosage-related overexpression. This is monogenic or structural-variant evidence, not GWAS.
findings.sourceQuote: This large series confirms the pathogenicity of COL4A1/2 duplications and triplications in adult-onset CSVD.

findings.causalEvidenceSummary: Established monogenic cause of CADASIL. This paper presents new genotype-phenotype data in 385 Taiwanese CADASIL patients carrying cysteine-altering NOTCH3 variants. Temporopolar WMH prevalence depended on the variant's EGFr risk category: 94.7% in HR, 54.4% in MR (mostly the p.R544C founder variant) and 33.3% in LR. HR-EGFr variant status was an independent predictor of temporopolar WMH, which was linked to greater WMH volume, more lacunes and more disability. This is not GWAS or MR evidence.
findings.sourceQuote: The prevalence of temporopolar WMH differed with the NOTCH3 risk category, being 94.7% in HR-EGFr, 54.4% in MR-EGFr, and 33.3% in LR-EGFr, compared with 31.9% in sporadic SVD without known pathogenic mutations ( Table 2 ).
